name: First Fort Dearborn — the covered way to the river, across the terrace
aka: Whistler's index no. 33, 'Covered Way to procure Water'

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: THE RANGE IS INFERRED, NOT DATED FOR THIS WORK. It opens on 25 January 1808, the date Whistler's draught carries, whose index names it; it may well be older. It closes on 16 August 1812 with the first fort, the day after the evacuation, when the post was burned (data/exclusions.json fort_dearborn_first_1803). Quaife's description of it ends 'Such was the old Fort previous to 1812', so nothing of it is carried to the second fort.

placement.position_note: INFERRED FROM TEXT, NEVER TRACED. The draught's index lists 'Covered Way to procure Water' and says it is 'Omited in their places', so the sheet does not draw it. Quaife p. 165: 'From the northeast corner of the stockade a covered way led to the river'. So the passage leaves the outer picket row's north-east corner (its record's footprint) along the frame's north, which is grid north, and runs to the committed 1812 water about 26.3 m off. Its runs, width and joints are data/traces/whistler_1808_fort_dearborn.json index no. 33 `seat`; tools/read_whistler_1808.py --check (run by check.sh) recomputes this corner, refuses a run more than one joint from the one before it or standing on more than 1.6 m of fall, and refuses the passage if its last run does not reach the water. The line and the runs are reconstructed (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-first-fort-water-2508).
placement.symbolic_location: North of the first Fort Dearborn's north-east angle: the run across the terrace, from the north-east angle to the head of the bank, 0.30-19.20 m north of the outer picket row's north face, its east row on the line of the east curtain. This record's origin is the run's south-west corner.

footprint.note: 3.0 m across, the narrowest the palisade archetype builds with a 1.5 m gateway at each end; no source gives the width. 18.90 m long, one of four runs: a structure stands on the lowest ground under it, so the passage is cut where the bank falls, and the ground falls 0.13 m under this one (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-first-fort-water-2508).

wall_kind.note: Quaife's covered way secured 'access in safety to the water in time of attack', which is read as screened. Built as two rows of the stockade's own pickets, open to the sky: no source says it was roofed, and none says it was not.

picket_height_m.note: Unattested; the outer row's twelve feet.

gate_sides.note: A passage is open at both ends. The archetype builds each run as an enclosure, so each end is a gateway between short returns of pickets. The postern through the two rows of the stockade into its south end is not built: the sheet omits the covered way and draws no opening there.

function.note: Index no. 33, 'Covered Way to procure Water'. Quaife p. 165: it led from the north-east corner of the stockade to the river, 'securing thus to the garrison access in safety to the water in time of attack'.

citations.citation: Quaife, Milo Milton. Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835: A Study of the Evolution of the Northwestern Frontier, together with a History of Fort Dearborn. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1913.
what_it_supplies: the 1808 Whistler draught index for the FIRST fort, with its scale and its distances
Major Long's 1816 report on the second fort under construction
a scholarly negative: no dimension of the second fort's stockade
what_it_does_not_supply: any plan or dimension of the 1816 fort

citations.citation: Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages.
what_it_supplies: the first fort's garrison in plan at a stated scale: the double row of pickets, the two blockhouses at the north-west and south-east angles, the four barracks ranges, the magazine, two small houses, the main gate, the parade and the flagstaff
the drafter's index of 34 numbered features, and the note that two of them (the covered way and the gutters) are omitted from their places
the arrangement of the factor's and agent's establishments, stables, gardens and the houses across the river, by position only and not to scale
what_it_does_not_supply: any building height: the folded elevations disagree with each other
the fort's bearing to true north: no north arrow was found on the reproduction
the covered way to the river and the gutters, which the index itself says are omitted
anything about the second fort of 1816

research_note: THE COVERED WAY, no. 33, built at T-2508 from Quaife's sentence: the run across the terrace, from the north-east angle to the head of the bank, run 1 of 4. The drafter letters 'wells' beside this same angle; no well is built from the word. Nobody is in it (L1).
